Overfill.Title: Overfill the container?
Overfill.Content: "{container}" is full. If you store "{item}" anyway, the container may tear and its contents scatter on the ground. Store it anyway?

Holds.ehlonna: ammunition, javelins and similar, and long weapons such as bows, spears or quarterstaffs

needleCase.Name: Needle Case
needleCase.Description: A slim case for blowgun needles. It holds up to 50 needles and nothing else.

slingPouch.Name: Sling Bullet Pouch
slingPouch.Description: A pouch for sling bullets. It holds up to 20 bullets and nothing else.

ammoPouch.Name: Ammunition Pouch
ammoPouch.Description: A pouch for firearm bullets. It holds up to 10 bullets and nothing else.

dartCase.Name: Dart Case
dartCase.Description: A case for darts. It holds up to 10 darts and nothing else.

javelinQuiver.Name: Javelin Quiver
javelinQuiver.Description: A quiver for javelins, worn on the back. It holds up to 5 javelins and nothing else.

knifeSheath.Name: Throwing Knife Sheath
knifeSheath.Description: A sheath for throwing knives and daggers. It holds up to 6 of them and nothing else.

enforceCapacity.Name: Enforce container capacity
enforceCapacity.Hint: Prevents stowing items if this would exceed a container’s weight or item count limit. Parent containers are checked too. Waterskin and ammunition container rules apply regardless of this setting.

notifyLevel.Name: Notifications
notifyLevel.Hint:
Important only: warnings (e.g. no room, out of range) and declined or cancelled trades
All: also messages about picking up, auto-stowing, tidying, completed trades and new log entries
Applies to all players and the GM.

overfillMode.Name: On overfill
overfillMode.Hint: "Block" rejects storing the item. "Overfill with tear risk" allows it with a warning. Each time something is stored in an overfilled container it may tear, scattering all of its contents on the map around the token.

overfillHardLimit.Name: Maximum overfill (%)
overfillHardLimit.Hint: Maximum percentage by which capacity may be exceeded, including in "Overfill with tear risk" mode. 0 = no limit.

tearChanceFactor.Name: Tear risk factor
tearChanceFactor.Hint: Tear chance in % = overfill in % × factor. With factor 1 a container overfilled by 25% tears with a 25% chance and always tears at 100% overfill or more.

ammoContainers.Name: Ammunition containers hold only their ammunition
ammoContainers.Hint: A quiver holds only arrows (up to 20); a crossbow bolt case holds only bolts (up to 20). A Quiver of Ehlonna can hold 60 arrows, bolts or similar ammunition, 18 javelins or similar items, and 6 long weapons such as bows, spears or quarterstaffs at the same time. Its contents are weightless. Arrows and crossbow bolts must be stowed in one of these suitable containers. The module’s additional ammunition containers also accept only their designated ammunition; using them is optional. All ammunition containers are worn on the body, cannot be stowed in other containers and cannot be overfilled. They therefore never tear.

enforceSlots.Name: Limit body slots
enforceSlots.Hint: Limits which and how many items may be carried directly in the inventory (outside of containers). Everything else must be stowed in containers.

slotActorTypes.Name: Slot limits apply to
slotActorTypes.Hint: Which actor types are affected by the body slot limits.

autoStow.Name: Auto-stow
autoStow.Hint: Automatically stows newly added items without a suitable body slot in the first suitable container with enough room. If none is available, the item is rejected. New containers themselves are not automatically stowed.

gmBypass.Name: Exempt the GM
gmBypass.Hint: The GM may ignore all limits.

fileLog.Name: Write the log
fileLog.Hint: Saves activities, character changes, warnings and errors in the "Pack & Ledger Logs" compendium. Only the GM can open it and read entries in the log window. New entries are saved only while a GM is logged in. Technical warnings from players are forwarded to the GM.

logRetentionDays.Name: Log retention (days)
logRetentionDays.Hint: Deletes older activity and coin log entries when the GM logs in. This value sets their maximum age in days. 0 = keep all entries.

limitWeapon.Name: Max weapons on the body
limitWeapon.Hint: Number of weapons that may be carried directly. Each weapon counts, also within a stack (5 longswords are 5 weapons). Daggers are the exception: two daggers share a slot (1 or 2 daggers take 1 slot, 3 or 4 take 2).

limitArmor.Name: Max armor on the body
limitArmor.Hint: Equipment of type light, medium or heavy armor.

limitTool.Name: Max tools on the body
limitTool.Hint: Items of type "Tool" (thieves' tools, artisan's tools, instruments …).

limitBackpack.Name: Max backpacks on the body
limitBackpack.Hint: Any container not recognized as a jug.

limitJug.Name: Max jugs on the body
limitJug.Hint: Containers whose name matches the jug pattern.

limitTrinket.Name: Max trinkets on the body
limitTrinket.Hint: Small items on the body: rings, spellcasting focuses, holy symbols, potions, healer's kits etc.

limitTrinketWeight.Name: Trinket weight limit (lb)
limitTrinketWeight.Hint:
Only items weighing less than this value per unit count as trinkets. Items at or above this weight must be stowed.
0 = no limit.

trinketEquipmentTypes.Name: Trinket: equipment types
trinketEquipmentTypes.Hint: Equipment types (dnd5e keys, separated by commas) that count as trinkets. Default: trinket, ring, rod, wand. Spellcasting focuses such as a crystal, orb, rod or wand have these types in dnd5e.

trinketConsumableTypes.Name: Trinket: consumable types
trinketConsumableTypes.Hint: Consumable types (separated by commas) that count as trinkets. Default: potion, trinket. This makes potions and the healer's kit count as trinkets.

trinketPattern.Name: Trinket: name pattern (regex)
trinketPattern.Hint: Items whose name matches this regular expression also count as trinkets regardless of type (e.g. Holy Symbol, Arcane Focus, Healer's Kit).

clothingPattern.Name: Clothing: name pattern (regex)
clothingPattern.Hint: Items whose name matches this regular expression count as clothing instead of trinkets. This applies even if they were imported e.g. as a consumable of type "trinket" (e.g. Robe, Vestments).

freePattern.Name: Free: name pattern (regex)
freePattern.Hint: Items whose name matches this regular expression take no slot and never need to be stowed. Natural weapons (type "Natural", e.g. Unarmed Strike, claws, bite) are always free.

bodyWeightEnabled.Name: Count body weight toward encumbrance
bodyWeightEnabled.Hint: Counts part of the character’s body weight as carried weight, so the encumbrance threshold is reached sooner. Uses the biography’s "Weight" field, e.g. "180 lb" or "82 kg".

bodyWeightPercent.Name: Body weight share (%)
bodyWeightPercent.Hint: Percentage of the body weight that counts toward the carried load. At 25% and 180 lb body weight, 45 lb count as carried.

jugPattern.Name: Jug pattern (regex)
jugPattern.Hint: Containers whose names match this regular expression count as jugs instead of backpacks. To change an individual item’s classification, right-click it and choose "Set inventory slot".

pilesEnabled.Name: Drop items onto the map
pilesEnabled.Hint: Items dragged from a sheet onto the map land on the ground as a pile. Double-click a pile to open it.

pileRange.Name: Pile reach (squares)
pileRange.Hint: How far a token may be from a pile to open it, take from it or drop something. 1 = adjacent. 0 = unlimited. Does not apply to the GM.

pileDeleteEmpty.Name: Remove empty piles
pileDeleteEmpty.Hint: Removes a pile from the map once its last item was taken.

pileMaskConsumables.Name: Mark potions and scrolls as unidentified
pileMaskConsumables.Hint: Potions and scrolls the GM puts into a pile from the sidebar or a compendium appear to players as “Unknown potion” or “Unknown scroll” until the GM identifies them. What players drop from their inventory stays as it is.

tradeEnabled.Name: Trading between characters
tradeEnabled.Hint: Adds a Trade button below the player list. Both sides put items and coins into a trade window; once both accept, everything is swapped. The GM trades for NPCs without a player.

tradeRange.Name: Trade range (squares)
tradeRange.Hint: How far apart the trading partners' tokens may be at most. 1 = adjacent. 0 = no limit. Does not apply when the GM trades on both sides.

pilePassiveDiscovery.Name: Passive Perception finds piles
pilePassiveDiscovery.Hint: When a player character moves within reach of a hidden pile and their passive Perception meets the DC, the pile becomes visible. Active Perception checks always work.

pileDiscoveryRange.Name: Discovery range (squares)
pileDiscoveryRange.Hint: How close a character must be to a hidden pile to discover it. 0 = unlimited.

pileDiscoveryDC.Name: Default discovery DC
pileDiscoveryDC.Hint: Perception DC for hidden piles that have no DC of their own set in the pile window.

pileLockDC.Name: Default lock DC
pileLockDC.Hint: DC of the thieves' tools check for chests that have no DC of their own set in the pile window.

currencyAudit.Name: Log coin changes
currencyAudit.Hint: Writes every coin change of a player character to the coin log: who, when, how much, before and after. Coins from item piles, trades and invoices are included.

currencyAuditGM.Name: Include the GM's changes
currencyAuditGM.Hint: Also logs coin changes made by the GM. Off: only changes by players.

currencyAskReason.Name: Ask for a reason
currencyAskReason.Hint: After a player changes coins, asks the GM for a reason, such as a reward or correction. The answer is saved in the log.

currencySuspiciousCount.Name: Suspicious change threshold
currencySuspiciousCount.Hint: This many changes by one player to the same character in a short time are flagged as suspicious (a warning in the log). 0 = never.

currencySuspiciousSeconds.Name: Suspicious change time window
currencySuspiciousSeconds.Hint: Time window in seconds for counting changes made by one player to the same character.

currencyMath.Name: Calculate with other denominations
currencyMath.Hint: Allows calculations using other denominations in coin fields, e.g. "-50 copper" in the gold field. dnd5e already supports entries such as "+10" and "-5" for the field’s own denomination.

currencyAutoConvert.Name: Make change automatically
currencyAutoConvert.Hint: If one denomination is insufficient, the module uses other coins and calculates change. The total value must cover the payment. Example: with 2 gp, entering "-5" in the silver field leaves 1 gp and 5 sp.

currencyPlatinum.Name: Change in platinum
currencyPlatinum.Hint: Allows platinum coins as change in coin fields and invoices. When disabled, no platinum is issued as change.

currencyElectrum.Name: Change in electrum
currencyElectrum.Hint: Change may be given in electrum.

invoicesEnabled.Name: Invoices
invoicesEnabled.Hint: The GM can send invoices to player characters (button in the token controls and in the header of the character sheet). The player pays or declines.

trackerEnabled.Name: Track characters
trackerEnabled.Hint: Writes changes to the stored data of player characters (hit points, spell slots, resources, inventory, item uses …) with the value before and after to the log (filter "Characters"). Coins are in the coin log.

trackerHideGM.Name: Hide the GM's changes
trackerHideGM.Hint: Do not log changes made by GMs or assistants.

trackerAllOwned.Name: Track all player-owned characters
trackerAllOwned.Hint: All characters a player owns. Off: only the assigned player characters. Unlinked tokens count as characters of their own.

trackerConcentration.Name: Track concentration
trackerConcentration.Hint: Log concentration effects and include them in the snapshot comparison.

trackerSpells.Name: Track spells
trackerSpells.Hint: Adds the spell associated with a spent spell slot to the log. If the module detects a spell that requires a slot without one being spent, it logs a warning.

trackerPrivate.Name: Include confidential fields
trackerPrivate.Hint: Also log and restore the confidential fields. They may contain personal text.

trackerPrivateFields.Name: Confidential fields
trackerPrivateFields.Hint: Comma-separated field paths, e.g. system.details.biography. These fields and their subfields are excluded while "Include confidential fields" is disabled.

provisionsEnabled.Name: Group provisions
provisionsEnabled.Hint: Shows the group's food and water (button in the token controls) and lets characters eat and drink from it during a long rest.

provisionsAuto.Name: Take automatically at a rest
provisionsAuto.Hint: Applies when a player starts a long rest on their own: whatever is missing is taken from the group's provisions without asking. Off: the player chooses in a dialog. At a rest the GM calls, the group shares out the meals together.

provisionsFoodPerDay.Name: Food per day
provisionsFoodPerDay.Hint: Rations a character needs a day.

provisionsWaterPerDay.Name: Water per day
provisionsWaterPerDay.Hint: Pints of water a character needs a day (a waterskin holds 4).

provisionsFoodPattern.Name: Food (name)
provisionsFoodPattern.Hint: Items whose name matches this regular expression count as food.

provisionsWaterPattern.Name: Water (name)
provisionsWaterPattern.Hint: Items whose name matches this regular expression count as water.

restEnabled.Name: Use the rest system
restEnabled.Hint: The GM calls rests with the button below the player list. At a long rest the characters eat and drink from the group's provisions.

restGMOnly.Name: Only the GM starts rests
restGMOnly.Hint: Players cannot rest on their own. Rests the GM calls and dnd5e's rest requests still work.

restAdvanceTime.Name: Advance world time
restAdvanceTime.Hint: Default when calling a rest: advances world time by the rest’s duration, according to the dnd5e rest variant.

restMealsPropose.Name: Propose meals automatically
restMealsPropose.Hint: Proposes a food and water allocation when the GM calls a long rest. When disabled, players allocate supplies themselves; the GM can request a proposal when needed.

restExternalFood.Name: External food source
restExternalFood.Hint: Share of the daily food requirement covered by an external source when enabled in the rest dialog. No items are consumed.

restExternalWater.Name: External water source
restExternalWater.Hint: Share of the daily water requirement covered by an external source when enabled in the rest dialog. No items are consumed.

restExhaustion.Name: Exhaustion from hunger and thirst
restExhaustion.Hint: Applies exhaustion from insufficient food or water during long rests. This section explains the rules; the thresholds and saving throw DC can be adjusted here.

restHalfWaterDC.Name: Saving throw DC for insufficient water
restHalfWaterDC.Hint: Constitution saving throw DC when a character has met at least half, but less than all, of their daily water requirement. 0 = no saving throw and no exhaustion from this check.

restNoFoodDays.Name: Days without food
restNoFoodDays.Hint: Formula for the number of days a character can go without food before gaining exhaustion. The formula can use the character’s data.

partyFund.Name: Group fund
partyFund.Hint: Reserves coins for shared purposes such as "General" or "Boat". Coins stay in the character’s purse. Use the character sheet or the group inventory’s "Group fund" tab to reserve, release or distribute them. Spending reserved coins displays a warning first. "Separate button" adds a coin pile button that reserves coins for "General". "Always" reserves all coins a group character takes from a pile. "Off" disables the group fund and its warnings.

general.Hint: Exemptions for the GM, notifications and the log.

containers.Name: Containers
containers.Hint: How much fits into backpacks, pouches and other containers, and what happens when they are overfilled.

slots.Name: Body slots
slots.Hint: What may be carried directly on the body. Everything else has to go into a container.

detection.Name: Detection
detection.Hint: How the module assigns items to body slots.

map.Hint: Item piles on the map and trading between characters.

weight.Name: Body weight
weight.Hint: Count part of the character's own body weight towards the carried load.

currency.Hint: Coin change logs, calculations in coin fields and invoices for players.

tracker.Hint: Track changes to player characters, save snapshots and restore them.

provisions.Hint: The group’s food and water, accompanying stores and meals during long rests.

Section.LimitsHint: How many items of each category can be carried directly on the body. Hover over a tile for details.
Section.TestHint: Enter an item name to see which patterns match. The first match wins.
Section.SecretsHint: In the pile window, the GM can hide a pile or give it a lock (it is then shown as a chest).
Section.CoinInput: Coin fields on the character sheet
Section.CoinChangeHint: Denominations used for change. Existing coins are preserved where possible.
Section.ProvisionsNeedHint: How much food and water a character needs each day.
Section.ProvisionsNamesHint: Food consumables are recognized by their "Nutritious" (food) and "Hydrating" (water) properties. Older dnd5e versions use the "food", "water" or "both" subtype. The module also checks the following name patterns for consumables and loot items. Patterns are regular expressions and are not case-sensitive.
Section.ProvisionsRestHint: dnd5e calculates recovery of hit points, hit dice, spell slots and uses. The GM calls a group rest with the button below the player list. During long rests, the group allocates food and water together. During short rests, a button can roll hit dice automatically.
Section.ProvisionsExhaustionHint: Less than half the water requirement causes one level of exhaustion, or two if already exhausted. At least half, but less than the full requirement calls for a Constitution save. Eating some food up to half the daily requirement counts as half a day without food; eating nothing counts as a whole day. Exceeding the configured limit causes exhaustion. With insufficient water or no more than half the food requirement, exhaustion is not reduced during that rest.

Session.Title: Meals at the rest
Session.Hint: Allocate food and water together. For each character, choose "Add a source", then select the source and quantity. Everyone must agree again after each change.
Session.Absent: Not with the group (their provisions do not count): {names}
Session.HintGM: No players are participating. Allocate food and water, then start the rest.
Session.Half: Daily requirement partly met. Water requires a Constitution save. Food up to and including half the daily requirement counts as half a day without food.
Session.RowShort: Only {amount} available: insufficient supplies or this source is not allowed.
Session.ProposeHint: Replaces the current allocation with a suggestion from the module. Everyone must agree again afterwards.
Session.ForceHint: Starts the rest now, even if not everyone has agreed.
Session.ForceConfirm: Not everyone has agreed yet: {names}. Start the rest anyway?
Session.StartHint: Hand out the food and water and start the rest.
Session.Running: Allocating supplies and starting the rest …
Session.Failed: The change could not be sent to the GM.
Session.NoSource: There is no further source for that.
Session.Open: Allocate food and water for the rest
Session.CarryFailed: Some meals could not be provided. Check the inventories and see the log for details.
Session.StartFailed: Some characters could not start their rest. Check the characters and see the log for details.
Session.Interrupted: Reloading the page interrupted the rest while supplies were being allocated. The rest has ended. Check the inventories and call another rest if needed.
Session.Replace: Supplies are still being allocated for another rest. Cancel that rest and call a new one?
Session.CancelStuck: Ends a stuck rest. Supplies already consumed are not refunded. Check the inventories afterwards.

Fund.DepositTooltip: Put coins into the group fund
Fund.NothingFree: All of {actor}’s coins are already reserved for the group fund.
Fund.NoDepositor: You have no character in the group whose coins you could put into the group fund.
Fund.DepositTitle: Put coins into the group fund
Fund.AccountDeleted: Purpose "{account}" removed. Its reserved coins are freely available again.
Fund.DeleteHint: The reserved coins stay with their respective characters and become freely available again.
Fund.DeleteConfirm: Remove purpose "{account}"? The reserved coins stay with their respective characters and become freely available again.
Fund.DepositHint: Coins stay in this character’s purse and are reserved for this purpose. You can release the reservation later by taking them out.
Fund.Deposited: {actor} put {coins} for "{account}" into the group fund.
Fund.WithdrawHint: The coins stay with {actor} and become freely available again.
Fund.Withdrawn: {actor} took {coins} for "{account}" out of the group fund.
Fund.NothingToWithdraw: {actor} has no coins in the group fund.
Fund.Holds: Coins reserved by {actor} for the group fund:
Fund.HoldsNothing: {actor} has nothing in the group fund.
Fund.Title: Group fund: {actor}
Fund.Tooltip: This share of the coin balance is reserved for the group fund. Click to put coins in or take them out.
Fund.SplitIntro: {coins} for "{account}" will be distributed equally among the {count} group characters. The preview shows each character’s share:
Fund.SplitRest: Only your own characters’ coins are distributed. Any remainder stays with the contributing character. The distributed coins are no longer reserved for the group fund.
Fund.AccountHint: The purpose these coins are reserved for. They stay in the character’s purse; spending them displays a warning first.
Fund.SpendTitle: Spend coins of the group fund?
Fund.SpendWarning: {actor} is about to use coins reserved for the following group fund purposes:
Fund.SpendHint: Continuing reduces the amount reserved for these purposes accordingly.
Fund.NothingToSplit: Your characters have no coins for "{account}" in the group fund. Only your own coins can be shared out.
Fund.NotEmpty: Coins are still reserved for "{account}". Only the GM can remove this purpose while it holds coins.
Fund.LogSpent: Spent from the group fund despite the warning: {spent}
Fund.SpendCancelled: Not paid: {actor} did not spend the coins of the group fund.
